EU.take: Posts are still growing parcels (Poste Italiane +11%, Geopost +8%, Austria and PostNord +9%) but almost none is growing profit: La Poste, PostNord, Austrian Post, CTT and Bnode all report lower operating earnings as letter decline, labour costs and parcel price competition outrun volume. The end of de minimis and new EU import fees are already visible in cross-border flows (PostNL international about -15%, CTT customs, InPost Poland marketplaces), while DHL is the outlier, with Express yield and tight air capacity lifting group EBIT 30%. Our read: scale in out-of-home and pricing power, not volume, now separates winners, and FedEx taking control of InPost confirms lockers are the strategic asset.

UK.take: UK parcel demand is growing (Royal Mail +7%, Evri +17% to over 1bn) but profit is migrating to asset-light, marketplace-fed networks: Evri earns about £400m EBITDA while Royal Mail sits around break-even under NICs, wage rises and USO reform. Our read: with FedEx now behind InPost/Yodel, the UK becomes a three-way out-of-home race and Royal Mail's delivery model reset before Christmas 2026 is the execution test to watch.
